Dear Ms. Bayoumi,

I acknowledge receipt of your email dated 4 October 2026, which you have characterized as a formal legal notice and as Orpita Community's final position concerning One More Day.

I reject the factual assertions, legal characterizations, demands, and conclusions contained in that notice.

Your correspondence repeatedly asserts that Orpita Community possesses exclusive rights and authority over my programming and game-design contributions. However, no instrument transferring those economic rights from me to Orpita has been identified or produced. Nor has Orpita established the factual prerequisites necessary for its reliance upon Article 138(4) and Article 175.

This response addresses each of the principal assertions in your notice.

Nothing in this correspondence constitutes an admission of Orpita Community's ownership, authorship, control, or authority over my independently created contributions. All rights, claims, defenses, objections, and remedies are expressly reserved.

1. The Characterization of One More Day as a Collective Work

Your primary assertion is that One More Day constitutes a collective work under Article 138(4), and that Orpita therefore possesses the rights contemplated by Article 175.

That characterization is expressly disputed.

The fact that the project was undertaken within a volunteer or educational community does not, by itself, establish that the resulting work satisfies the statutory definition of a collective work.

Likewise, the existence of multiple contributors does not, by itself, establish that Orpita was the directing entity contemplated by the law.

The relevant factual circumstances of creation must be established.

In particular, your notice does not identify any contemporaneous agreement, project document, contractual instrument, or other evidence establishing that Orpita directed and supervised the creation of One More Day in the manner required for the statutory characterization upon which you rely.

The contemporaneous development evidence instead demonstrates that I exercised substantial and direct responsibility over the development process.

I possess, among other evidence:

contemporaneous Miro project-management records dated 31 July 2025;

Git/version-control history documenting the development chronology and my direct technical contribution, including the 3 September 2025 version;

records demonstrating delegation of development responsibilities;

records of project organization and task allocation; and

development decisions and coordination undertaken during the actual creation of the project.

image.pngimage.png
The Miro record is contemporaneous evidence of the development structure and demonstrates my role in organizing the project, delegating responsibilities, and directing development activities.

The Git history independently documents the chronology of implementation and my direct participation in creating the software.

These records were not created after the present dispute arose. They originate from the actual development period and therefore provide contemporaneous evidence concerning how the project was managed and created.

I do not suggest that the existence of my management role, standing alone, automatically determines the legal classification of the entire work. Rather, it establishes factual circumstances directly relevant to your assertion that Orpita was the directing entity.

If Orpita maintains that it was nevertheless the directing entity contemplated by Article 138(4) and Article 175, please identify the contemporaneous evidence establishing:

the authority by which Orpita directed the development;

the instructions issued by Orpita concerning my programming or game-design work;

the supervision exercised by Orpita over that work;

the agreement or organizational instrument under which such authority existed;

when that authority was established; and

how that authority was actually exercised during development.

A present-day characterization of Orpita's role cannot substitute for evidence establishing the actual circumstances of creation.

2. My Role and the Existence of Other Developers

Your notice states that I was a former Founder of the Community and Head of Game Development and that other developers also participated in the project.

I do not dispute that other persons participated.

That fact, however, does not establish the proposition you seek to derive from it.

The existence of multiple developers does not establish that Orpita acquired ownership of the code created by each developer, nor does it extinguish the rights of an author in independently created material.

Your assertion that I "did not write the entire codebase alone" is therefore legally insufficient to establish that Orpita owns or controls the programming that I personally authored.

If Orpita disputes my authorship of any particular portion of the programming, identify specifically:

the relevant code;

the person whom you contend authored it;

the evidence supporting that attribution;

the date of its creation; and

the legal instrument by which the relevant economic rights were transferred to Orpita.

The Git history provides objective evidence concerning authorship, chronology, and implementation and will be relied upon where necessary.

The issue is not whether other developers participated in One More Day. The issue is whether Orpita possesses the legal rights you claim over the particular contributions at issue.

You have not established that proposition.

3. The Contributions of Artists, Musicians, and Designers

Your notice identifies various individuals who contributed artwork, music, sound, and game-design material.

Again, I do not dispute that other contributors participated.

However, identifying the creators of those materials does not establish that Orpita owns their rights.

If those individuals retained their respective copyrights, their rights remain theirs unless validly transferred or licensed.

If Orpita claims that it acquired those rights, identify the instruments by which those rights were acquired.

More importantly, the rights of those contributors do not automatically become rights of Orpita merely because their work formed part of the project.

There must be a legal basis for the claimed transfer, assignment, or authorization.

Your notice identifies none.

My position concerning the rebuilt version is also straightforward: it does not incorporate the artwork, music, sound effects, or other creative assets identified in your notice.

Accordingly, the mere existence of those contributions does not establish infringement by a separately implemented version that does not reproduce them.

4. Article 140 and the Assertion That the Rebuilt Version Is a Derivative Work

You state categorically that my rebuilt version is a derivative work.

I reject that characterization.

The fact that a new version concerns the same game project does not, without more, establish that protected expression from the original work has been reproduced.

A derivative-work claim requires identification of the protected material allegedly carried into the subsequent work.

Your notice identifies no such material.

You have not identified:

the protected work allegedly incorporated;

the protected expression allegedly reproduced;

the precise portion of my rebuilt version allegedly containing that expression;

the author or rights holder of that expression; or

the legal basis upon which Orpita claims the right to enforce that particular right.

Instead, your notice relies upon the general proposition that a rebuilt version cannot extinguish rights in an original work.

I do not contend otherwise.

My position is that the rebuilt version does not reproduce the protected expression of the other contributors.

A general statement concerning derivative works does not establish that a particular independently implemented work is infringing.

5. Article 141 and Unprotected Ideas, Systems, and Methods of Operation

Article 141 is directly relevant to this dispute.

The provision excludes mere ideas, procedures, systems, methods of operation, concepts, principles, discoveries, and data from copyright protection.

Accordingly, similarities in gameplay concepts, mechanics, systems, rules, functional behavior, procedures, or methods of operation cannot by themselves establish copyright infringement.

If Orpita's objection to the rebuilt version concerns similarities in gameplay mechanics, functionality, systems, or ideas, such similarities must be distinguished from protected expression.

My rebuilt implementation is independently written and does not use the artwork, music, sound effects, or other protected creative assets belonging to the contributors identified in your notice.

If you contend that protected expression nevertheless appears in the rebuilt version, identify it specifically.

6. Article 149 and the Absence of a Written Transfer From Me

Your reliance upon Article 149 raises a fundamental issue for Orpita.

You repeatedly demand that I produce written authority from other contributors.

The same requirement must be applied to Orpita's own claim.

If Orpita claims that it owns or exclusively controls my economic rights, identify the written instrument, signed by me, by which those rights were transferred.

Article 149 requires the transfer of economic rights to be made in writing and to identify the rights concerned, together with the scope, purpose, duration, and place of exploitation.

No such instrument has been identified in your notice.

Accordingly, please produce the alleged written transfer by which I assigned my economic rights in my programming and game-design contributions to Orpita.

If you rely upon a LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING document, community policy, or other document, identify:

its date;

its parties;

the provision allegedly applicable to me;

the economic rights allegedly transferred;

the duration;

the territorial scope;

the purpose of exploitation; and

the basis upon which you contend it constitutes a valid transfer of rights already created.

A document created after completion of the project cannot simply be characterized as proof of a historical transfer of rights without establishing its legal effect and applicability to the relevant work.

7. Article 174 and Independent Exploitation

You rely upon Article 174 to assert that I cannot independently exploit my contribution.

Your characterization omits the statutory distinction concerning contributions belonging to different categories of art.

Article 174 expressly addresses circumstances in which contributions belong to different categories of art and provides for independent exploitation of such contributions, subject to the statutory conditions and unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Your notice identifies programming, artwork, music, sound, and game-design contributions as belonging to different categories.

You have nevertheless identified no written agreement by which I agreed to surrender or restrict the rights applicable to my independently distinguishable contributions.

Your blanket assertion that I therefore have no authority to independently exploit my programming and game-design contributions is consequently rejected.

If Orpita contends that Article 174(2) does not apply, identify the precise statutory basis and factual circumstances upon which that contention rests.

8. The Alleged Absence of Authority From Other Contributors

Your notice states that I possess no written consent from numerous contributors.

That assertion assumes that such consent is legally required for the particular activity at issue.

It also assumes that the rebuilt version exploits the protected expression of each of those contributors.

Neither proposition has been established.

I am not seeking to appropriate or publish another contributor's artwork, music, sound effects, or other protected material.

The relevant distinction is between:

the independent implementation of programming and design,

and

the reproduction or exploitation of another person's protected expression.

If you allege that a specific contributor's protected expression is incorporated into the rebuilt version, identify that expression.

If you further contend that Orpita owns or controls that contributor's rights, identify the instrument by which Orpita acquired them.

The mere existence of a list of contributors is not evidence of either proposition.

9. The Alleged "Established Community Practice"

Your reference to an alleged community practice concerning administrative access is irrelevant to the question of copyright ownership.

An administrative-access practice does not constitute an assignment of economic rights.

Nor does an offer to provide administrative access establish that Orpita possesses ownership over my contributions.

If Orpita relies upon a contractual term or binding community agreement restricting my economic rights, produce the document and identify the specific provision upon which you rely.

An alleged customary practice cannot substitute for the statutory requirements governing the transfer or restriction of economic rights.

10. Your "Cumulative" Legal Position

You state that Orpita relies cumulatively upon Articles 138(4), 140, 149, 174, and 175.

Citing multiple provisions does not cure the absence of evidence establishing the factual prerequisites of those provisions.

Each legal theory requires its own factual foundation.

If Orpita relies upon Article 175, it must establish the statutory basis for treating the work as a collective work and establish Orpita's status as the relevant directing entity.

If Orpita relies upon Article 174, it must address the statutory rules governing joint authorship and contributions belonging to different categories of art.

If Orpita relies upon Article 140, it must identify the protected expression allegedly incorporated into the rebuilt version.

If Orpita relies upon Article 149, it must identify the written instrument transferring the relevant economic rights.

The cumulative citation of provisions does not eliminate these requirements.

11. Your Assertion Concerning the Burden of Proof

Your statement that the burden of proof necessarily lies upon me because I challenge copyright validity is rejected as an inaccurate characterization of the dispute.

I am not challenging the validity of every copyright interest held by every individual contributor.

I am challenging Orpita's assertion that Orpita itself possesses the legal authority to control my independently created programming and game-design contributions and to prevent their independent exploitation.

That is a specific claim of ownership and authority.

If Orpita asserts that it acquired those rights from me, identify the transfer.

If Orpita asserts that it possesses those rights by operation of Article 175, establish the factual and legal basis for the collective-work characterization and Orpita's status as the relevant directing entity.

If Orpita asserts that the rebuilt version infringes another person's rights, identify the protected expression allegedly infringed.

The burden cannot be shifted merely by describing my position as a challenge to copyright validity.

12. The Proposed Settlement

I reject the settlement proposal.

The proposal does not resolve the underlying legal issue and instead conditions my ability to present my own development work upon permission from Orpita.

I do not accept that premise.

In particular, I reject any arrangement under which:

Orpita's alleged ownership of my contributions is implicitly acknowledged;

my ability to showcase my own work is treated as a permission granted by Orpita;

my programming and design contributions are reduced to an administrative portfolio permission; or

acceptance of the proposal could subsequently be relied upon as an admission of Orpita's ownership or control.

The proposed administrative access, portfolio limitations, code-excerpt restrictions, and credit designation are therefore rejected.

13. Your October 11 Deadline

I reject the unilateral deadline of 11 October 2026.

A deadline contained in a unilateral legal notice does not create a contractual or statutory obligation where none otherwise exists.

Nor will failure to accept your proposed settlement by that date constitute an admission of any assertion contained in your notice.

I will not provide an undertaking that presupposes Orpita's ownership or authority where that ownership or authority has not been established.

14. DMCA and Other Enforcement Threats

Your reference to immediate DMCA takedown notices and other enforcement action is noted and rejected insofar as it is premised upon the unsupported assertions contained in your notice.

A takedown request does not establish ownership or infringement.

Any enforcement action concerning material independently created by me will be evaluated on the basis of the actual authorship, ownership, licensing history, and content of the material concerned.

I expressly reserve all rights and remedies arising from any inaccurate, unsupported, or improper enforcement action.

15. Formal Demand for Substantiation

Your notice repeatedly demands that I substantiate my position.

I am prepared to substantiate my position with contemporaneous development evidence.

At the same time, Orpita must substantiate the affirmative legal claims made in its own notice.

Accordingly, please provide:

The written instrument, signed by me, by which Orpita acquired any economic rights in my programming or game-design contributions;

The contemporaneous evidence establishing that Orpita was the directing entity contemplated by Article 138(4) and Article 175 during the actual creation of One More Day;

The agreement, policy, or other binding instrument under which I allegedly surrendered, assigned, licensed, or restricted my economic rights;

If Orpita alleges that my rebuilt version reproduces protected expression belonging to another contributor, identification of each allegedly protected work and the precise expression allegedly reproduced;

If Orpita claims rights belonging to any of the contributors identified in your notice, the instrument by which those rights were transferred or licensed to Orpita;

The specific factual and legal basis for your assertion that Article 174 prevents the independent exploitation of my programming and game-design contributions; and

The evidence supporting your assertion that I did not author the particular programming contributions at issue.

I require your response to these demands within 7 days.

For the avoidance of doubt, my position remains that I retain the rights applicable to my independently created contributions, subject to the rights, if any, of other authors in their respective works.

I reject Orpita's unsupported assertion that its status as a community, its hosting of the project, its administrative access to an itch.io page, or its alleged community practices establish ownership or exclusive control over my contributions.

The contemporaneous development record will be relied upon to establish the actual structure of the project's development and the respective roles of the participants.

Nothing in this correspondence grants Orpita any license, assignment, consent, authorization, acknowledgment of ownership, or other right that it does not otherwise possess.

Nothing herein constitutes a waiver of any right, claim, defense, remedy, or objection available to me.

All rights are expressly reserved.

Sincerely,

Youssef Amr

fragments.content: لقد حصلت على نتائج البحث. الآن أحتاج إلى فتح بعض هذه النتائج للحصول على النصوص الكاملة للمواد القانونية.

لقد حصلت على نصوص المواد القانونية. الآن أحتاج إلى تحليلها وصياغة الرد.

**تحليل إيميل يوسف:**

إيميل يوسف قوي جداً، وهو يرد على كل نقطة في إيميلنا السابق. النقاط الرئيسية:

1.  **يرفض وصف المشروع بأنه "مصنف جماعي" (Collective Work):** يجادل بأن مجرد كون المشروع تطوعياً أو تعليمياً لا يجعله مصنفاً جماعياً. ويطلب دليلاً على أن Orpita كانت "الجهة الموجهة" (directing entity). ويقدم أدلة (Miro, Git history) على أنه هو من كان يدير التطوير.

2.  **ينفي ادعاءنا بأنه "المطور الوحيد":** يقول إنه لم يدّعِ ذلك أبداً، وأن وجود مطورين آخرين لا يعني أن Orpita تملك الكود الذي كتبه هو شخصياً.

3.  **ينفي أن يكون قد استخدم أعمال الفنانين والموسيقيين:** يقول إن نسخته المعاد بناؤها لا تتضمن فنهم أو موسيقاهم. وبالتالي، لا يحتاج إذنهم.

4.  **يرفض وصف نسخته بأنها "عمل مشتق" (Derivative Work):** يجادل بأن مجرد كونه لعبة جديدة في نفس المشروع لا يجعلها عملاً مشتقاً. ويطلب منا تحديد التعبير المحمي الذي تم نسخه.

5.  **يستشهد بالمادة 141:** يذكر أن المادة 141 تحمي "الأفكار والإجراءات وأساليب العمل وطرق التشغيل" من الحماية. ويقول إن أي تشابه في آليات اللعب أو الأنظمة لا يشكل انتهاكاً لحقوق النشر.

6.  **يقلب المادة 149 ضدنا:** يطالبنا نحن بتقديم عقد نقل مكتوب موقّع منه، ينقل حقوقه الاقتصادية إلى Orpita. وبما أننا لا نملك هذا العقد، فإنه يحتفظ بحقوقه.

7.  **يستشهد بالمادة 174 (فقرة الاستغلال المستقل):** يستشهد بالجزء الذي يقول إنه إذا كانت المساهمات من "فئات فنية مختلفة" (مثل البرمجة مقابل الفن)، يمكن لكل مؤلف استغلال الجزء الخاص به بشكل مستقل. ويجادل بأن برمجته هي فئة فنية مختلفة.

8.  **يؤكد أنه لا يحتاج إذن المساهمين الآخرين:** لأنه لا يستخدم أعمالهم.

9.  **يرفض "العرف المجتمعي" (Community Practice):** يقول إن الوصول الإداري لا يعني نقل الحقوق.

10. **يرفض الموقف التراكمي:** يقول إن الاستشهاد بمواد متعددة لا يعفي من إثبات المتطلبات الواقعية لكل منها.

11. **يرفض تحميلنا عبء الإثبات:** يقول إنه لا يطعن في صحة حقوق النشر، بل يطعن في ادعاء Orpita بامتلاك حقوق مساهماته.

12. **يرفض عرض التسوية:** لأنه يعترف ضمنياً بملكية Orpita.

13. **يرفض الموعد النهائي:** ويقول إنه لا يخلق التزاماً.

14. **يرفض تهديدات DMCA:** ويحتفظ بحقوقه.

15. **يطلب منا الإثبات:** يطلب منا تقديم عقد نقل موقّع منه، ودليل على أن Orpita كانت "الجهة الموجهة"، وأي اتفاق يزعم أن حقوقه نُقلت أو قُيدت.

**نقاط ضعف إيميل يوسف:**

*   **الادعاء بأنه هو "الجهة الموجهة":** هو يقدم أدلة على أنه كان يدير التطوير (Miro, Git)، لكن هذا لا يعني أن Orpita لم تكن "الجهة الموجهة". يمكن القول إن Orpita كانت "الجهة الموجهة" على مستوى أعلى (تحديد الرؤية، تنظيم الـ Game Jam، النشر)، بينما كان يوسف يدير التنفيذ اليومي.
*   **تفسير المادة 174:** هو يفسر "فئات فنية مختلفة" على أنها تعني أن البرمجة تختلف عن الفن. هذا صحيح، لكن الفقرة تقول "بشرط ألا يضر ذلك باستغلال المصنف المشترك". يمكن القول إن نشر نسخة منافسة كاملة يضر باستغلال العمل المشترك.
*   **تفسير المادة 141:** صحيح أن الأفكار غير محمية، لكن التعبير عن هذه الأفكار (الكود المحدد، بنية اللعبة، السرد) محمي. نحتاج إلى تحديد التعبير المحمي الذي تم نسخه.
*   **ادعاؤه بأنه لا يستخدم فن الآخرين:** هذا ادعاء واقعي، لكنه يحتاج إلى إثبات. يمكن أن نطلب منه تقديم قائمة بما تتضمنه نسخته.

**نقاط قوتنا:**

*   **المادة 175:** إذا أثبتنا أن Orpita هي "الجهة الموجهة" للمصنف الجماعي، فإنها تملك الحق الحصري. لدينا أدلة على أن Orpita نظمت الـ Game Jam، وحددت الرؤية، ونشرت اللعبة.
*   **المادة 149:** ينطبق على نقل الحقوق. نحن لا ندعي أن يوسف نقل حقوقه إلينا، بل ندعي أننا نملك الحقوق كـ "مصنف جماعي" بموجب المادة 175. لذا، لا نحتاج إلى عقد نقل منه.
*   **المادة 140:** حتى لو كانت نسخته "جديدة"، فهي مبنية على عمل موجود، وبالتالي فهي "عمل مشتق" بموجب التعريف الواسع في المادة 138(6). المادة 140 تحمي العمل الأصلي.
*   **حجتنا الأخلاقية:** يوسف كان جزءاً من فريق تطوعي، ويحاول الآن الاستيلاء على عمل جماعي ونشره بشكل فردي. هذا يتعارض مع روح المجتمع.

**استراتيجية الرد:**

1.  **الرد على الادعاء بأن المشروع ليس "مصنفاً جماعياً":** نؤكد أن Orpita كانت "الجهة الموجهة" لأنها:
    *   نظمت المشاركة في GMTK Game Jam.
    *   حددت الرؤية العامة للعبة.
    *   نشرت اللعبة باسمها على itch.io.
    *   كان لديها هيكل إداري (Founder, Head of Game Development, etc.).
    *   نطلب منه تقديم دليل على أنه هو "الجهة الموجهة" وليس مجرد مدير تنفيذي.

2.  **الرد على حجة "فئات فنية مختلفة" (المادة 174):** نؤكد أن الاستغلال المستقل مسموح به **"بشرط ألا يضر ذلك باستغلال المصنف المشترك"**. نشر نسخة كاملة من اللعبة على itch.io الخاص به، حتى لو كانت مجانية، ينافس اللعبة الأصلية ويضر باستغلالها. وبالتالي، لا ينطبق الاستثناء.

3.  **الرد على حجة "الأفكار غير محمية" (المادة 141):** نوافق على أن الأفكار غير محمية، لكننا نؤكد أن **التعبير** عن هذه الأفكار محمي. الكود المحدد، والبنية الفريدة للعبة، والسرد، كلها تعبيرات محمية. نطلب منه تقديم قائمة بما تتضمنه نسخته، ونحتفظ بحقنا في تقييم ما إذا كان هذا التعبير ينتهك حقوقنا.

4.  **الرد على طلب الإثبات (المادة 149):** نوضح أننا لا نعتمد على المادة 149 للحصول على الحقوق من يوسف. نحن نعتمد على المادة 175، التي تمنح الحقوق للكيان الموجه. وبالتالي، لا نحتاج إلى عقد نقل منه. ومع ذلك، نطلب منه تقديم أي عقد ينقل حقوقه، إن وجد، لإثبات أنه لا يملك الحقوق.

5.  **طلب الإثبات المضاد:** نطلب منه:
    *   تقديم قائمة مفصلة بكل ما تتضمنه نسخته المعاد بناؤها، مع تحديد أي عناصر من اللعبة الأصلية.
    *   تقديم دليل على أنه هو "الجهة الموجهة" للمشروع، وليس مجرد مدير.
    *   تقديم أي اتفاق مكتوب يزعم أنه يمنحه الحق في نشر نسخة مستقلة.

6.  **التأكيد على الموقف:** نوضح أننا نملك الحقوق بموجب القانون، وأن أي نشر بدون إذن سيعرضه للمسؤولية القانونية.

**صياغة الرد:**

سأكتب رداً باللغة العربية، بأسلوب قانوني رسمي، يعالج كل نقطة من نقاط يوسف، ويؤكد على موقفنا. سأستخدم أرقام المواد ونصوصها لدعم حججنا.

سأبدأ بالرد على الادعاءات الواقعية، ثم أنتقل إلى الادعاءات القانونية.

**نقاط رئيسية في الرد:**

*   **المقدمة:** نرفض كل ادعاءات يوسف.
*   **الرد على "المصنف الجماعي":** نؤكد أن Orpita هي "الجهة الموجهة" لأنها نظمت ووجهت المشروع. نطلب منه تقديم دليل على العكس.
*   **الرد على "المطور الوحيد":** نوضح أننا لم ندّعِ أنه المطور الوحيد، لكن هذا لا يعني أنه يملك الحقوق الحصرية.
*   **الرد على "فئات فنية مختلفة":** نؤكد أن الاستغلال المستقل محظور إذا كان يضر بالعمل المشترك. نشر نسخة كاملة يضر بالعمل المشترك.
*   **الرد على "الأفكار غير محمية":** نوافق على أن الأفكار غير محمية، لكن التعبير محمي. نطلب منه تحديد ما إذا كان قد نسخ أي تعبير محمي.
*   **الرد على "المادة 149":** نوضح أننا لا نحتاج إلى عقد نقل منه، لأننا نعتمد على المادة 175.
*   **طلب الإثبات:** نطلب منه تقديم قائمة مفصلة بما تتضمنه نسخته، ودليل على أنه "الجهة الموجهة"، وأي اتفاق يزعم أنه يمنحه الحق في النشر.
*   **الخاتمة:** نؤكد على موقفنا ونحتفظ بحقوقنا.

سأحرص على أن يكون الرد حازماً لكن مهنياً. سأستخدم لغة قانونية دقيقة.

الآن، سأكتب الرد.

This is a strong and detailed legal response from Youssef. He has raised several substantive points, and we need to address them carefully. Below is a point-by-point rebuttal that reinforces our position, corrects his misinterpretations of the law, and places the burden of proof back on him.

---

**Subject: Re: One More Day — Response to Your Correspondence of 4 October**

---

Dear Youssef,

I have reviewed your correspondence. I will address your points directly.

**1. The Characterization of One More Day as a Collective Work**

You dispute that One More Day is a collective work under Article 138(4). You are correct that the mere existence of a volunteer or educational community does not, by itself, establish the statutory definition. However, you overlook the factual circumstances that do.

Article 138(4) defines a collective work as one "made by more than one author under the guidance of a natural or juridical person, who shall undertake publishing the work in his name and under his supervision." Orpita Community organized the project, directed its development, and published the game under its name on the official itch.io page. The contributions of all participants, including yourself, were integrated into the general objective set by the Community.

You assert that your Miro records and Git history demonstrate that *you* were the directing entity. I disagree. Those records demonstrate that you exercised *managerial* responsibility over the development process. They do not establish that you were the *directing entity* contemplated by Article 138(4). The directing entity is the one that undertakes publication under its name and supervision—that is Orpita Community. You were the Head of Game Development, not the publisher or the ultimate authority.

If you maintain that Orpita was not the directing entity, please identify the contemporaneous evidence establishing:

- The authority by which Orpita directed the development;
- The instructions issued by Orpita concerning your programming or game-design work;
- The supervision exercised by Orpita over that work;
- The agreement or organizational instrument under which such authority existed;
- When that authority was established; and
- How that authority was actually exercised during development.

A present-day characterization of your role cannot substitute for evidence establishing the actual circumstances of creation.

**2. Your Role and the Existence of Other Developers**

You state that you do not dispute that other developers participated. That is correct. However, your argument that the existence of multiple developers does not establish that Orpita acquired ownership of the code created by each developer misses the point.

Under Article 175, the natural or legal person under whose direction the *collective work* was created holds the exclusive right to exercise the author's rights over that work. The collective work is the game as a whole. Your individual contribution is part of that collective work. You cannot separate your contribution from the collective work to which it belongs.

If you dispute my authorship of any particular portion of the programming, identify specifically:

- The relevant code;
- The person whom you contend authored it;
- The evidence supporting that attribution;
- The date of its creation; and
- The legal instrument by which the relevant economic rights were transferred to Orpita.

The Git history you rely upon may document authorship, but it does not establish that you retained independent economic rights. Authorship and ownership are distinct legal concepts.

**3. The Contributions of Artists, Musicians, and Designers**

You state that you do not dispute that other contributors participated. However, you argue that identifying the creators of those materials does not establish that Orpita owns their rights.

This is correct. However, it is also irrelevant to the central issue. The issue is not whether Orpita owns the rights of the artists, musicians, and designers. The issue is whether *you* have the right to publish a derivative version of the game that incorporates their work.

You state that your rebuilt version does not incorporate the artwork, music, sound effects, or other creative assets identified in my notice. If that is true, then you should have no objection to stating, item by item, what your rebuilt version *does* contain from the original game. I request that you do so.

**4. Article 140 and the Assertion That the Rebuilt Version Is a Derivative Work**

You reject the characterization of your rebuilt version as a derivative work. However, Article 138(6) defines a derivative work as "the work that originates from a preexisting work." Your rebuilt version originates from the original One More Day game. It is therefore a derivative work.

You demand that I identify the protected expression allegedly carried into your subsequent work. I have already done so: the artwork, music, sound effects, narrative, game design, and code created by the other contributors. You claim that your rebuilt version does not incorporate these elements. If that is true, then you should have no objection to providing a detailed description of what your rebuilt version does contain. I request that you do so.

**5. Article 141 and Unprotected Ideas, Systems, and Methods of Operation**

You are correct that Article 141 excludes mere ideas, procedures, systems, methods of operation, concepts, principles, discoveries, and data from copyright protection. However, you overlook the fact that Article 141 also states that protection "shall not cover the following: (1) Official documents..."

Article 141 does not assist your position. The code you wrote, the specific implementation of game mechanics, the narrative structure, and the creative expression embodied in the game are protected. Your argument that similarities in gameplay mechanics, functionality, systems, or ideas cannot establish infringement is correct as a matter of law. However, it is irrelevant because my objection is not based on similarities in ideas. It is based on the reproduction of protected expression.

If you contend that your rebuilt version does not reproduce protected expression, identify precisely what it does contain.

**6. Article 149 and the Absence of a Written Transfer From You**

You correctly state that Article 149 requires the transfer of economic rights to be made in writing and to identify the rights concerned, together with the scope, purpose, duration, and place of exploitation.

I am not relying on Article 149 to establish Orpita's ownership of your contributions. I am relying on Article 175. Under Article 175, the natural or legal person under whose direction the collective work was created holds the exclusive right to exercise the author's rights over that work. No written transfer from you is required for Orpita to exercise those rights.

Your reliance on Article 149 is misplaced. You are the one who has not produced a written transfer. You have no written authority from the other contributors. You cannot exploit their work.

**7. Article 174 and Independent Exploitation**

You rely on Article 174 to assert that you have the right to exploit your contribution independently. You quote the provision concerning contributions belonging to different categories of art.

Article 174 states: "However, if the contribution of each belongs to a different category of art, each co-author shall have the right to exploit independently his part, without prejudice to the exploitation of the work of joint authorship, unless otherwise agreed in writing."

You overlook the condition: "without prejudice to the exploitation of the work of joint authorship." Your proposed publication of a rebuilt version of the entire game on your own itch.io page would directly compete with the official version. This prejudices the exploitation of the work of joint authorship. Therefore, your independent exploitation is not permitted.

**8. The Alleged Absence of Authority From Other Contributors**

You state that you are not seeking to appropriate or publish another contributor's artwork, music, sound effects, or other protected material. If that is true, then you should have no objection to providing a detailed statement of what your rebuilt version does contain. I request that you do so.

If you allege that a specific contributor's protected expression is *not* incorporated into the rebuilt version, you are free to provide evidence to that effect. Until you do, the presumption is that your rebuilt version incorporates their work.

**9. The Alleged "Established Community Practice"**

You state that an administrative-access practice does not constitute an assignment of economic rights. That is correct. I have never suggested that it does. The practice is relevant only to the settlement offer, not to the question of ownership.

**10. Your "Cumulative" Legal Position**

You state that citing multiple provisions does not cure the absence of evidence. I agree. That is why I have provided evidence for each provision:

- Under Article 138(4) and 175: the Community organized the project, directed its development, and published the game under its name.
- Under Article 174: even if joint authorship, you may not exploit the work without written consent.
- Under Article 140: your rebuilt version is a derivative work.
- Under Article 149: you have no written authority from the other contributors.

**11. Your Assertion Concerning the Burden of Proof**

You state that you are not challenging the validity of every copyright interest held by every individual contributor. You are challenging Orpita's assertion that it possesses the legal authority to control your independently created contributions.

That is a specific claim. If Orpita asserts that it acquired those rights from you, identify the transfer. Orpita asserts that it possesses those rights by operation of Article 175. The factual and legal basis for the collective-work characterization is set out above.

**12. The Proposed Settlement**

You reject the settlement proposal. I note your rejection.

The proposal was made in good faith. It remains open.

**13. Your October 11 Deadline**

You reject the unilateral deadline of 11 October 2026. I note your rejection.

**14. DMCA and Other Enforcement Threats**

You state that a takedown request does not establish ownership or infringement. That is correct. However, a takedown request is a procedural mechanism, not a final adjudication. If you publish a derivative version of One More Day without authorization, Orpita will file a DMCA takedown notice with the hosting platform. The platform will then determine whether to remove the content.

**15. Formal Demand for Substantiation**

You request that Orpita substantiate its claims. I have done so above.

You also request that I provide:

- The written instrument, signed by you, by which Orpita acquired any economic rights in your programming or game-design contributions;
- The contemporaneous evidence establishing that Orpita was the directing entity;
- The agreement, policy, or other binding instrument under which you allegedly surrendered, assigned, licensed, or restricted your economic rights;
- If Orpita alleges that your rebuilt version reproduces protected expression belonging to another contributor, identification of each allegedly protected work and the precise expression allegedly reproduced;
- If Orpita claims rights belonging to any of the contributors identified in my notice, the instrument by which those rights were transferred or licensed to Orpita;
- The specific factual and legal basis for your assertion that Article 174 prevents the independent exploitation of your programming and game-design contributions; and
- The evidence supporting your assertion that you did not author the particular programming contributions at issue.

I have addressed these points above. Orpita does not rely on a written transfer from you. Orpita relies on Article 175.

I require your response to these demands within 7 days.

Sincerely,

**Elham Bayoumi**
Legal Advisor
Orpita Community
orpitastudios@gmail.com

Dear Ms. Bayoumi,

I acknowledge receipt of your email dated 4 October 2026, which you have characterized as a formal legal notice and as Orpita Community's final position concerning One More Day.

I reject the factual assertions, legal characterizations, demands, and conclusions contained in that notice.

Your correspondence repeatedly asserts that Orpita Community possesses exclusive rights and authority over my programming and game-design contributions. However, no instrument transferring those economic rights from me to Orpita has been identified or produced. Nor has Orpita established the factual prerequisites necessary for its reliance upon Article 138(4) and Article 175.

This response addresses each of the principal assertions in your notice.

Nothing in this correspondence constitutes an admission of Orpita Community's ownership, authorship, control, or authority over my independently created contributions. All rights, claims, defenses, objections, and remedies are expressly reserved.

1. The Characterization of One More Day as a Collective Work

Your primary assertion is that One More Day constitutes a collective work under Article 138(4), and that Orpita therefore possesses the rights contemplated by Article 175.

That characterization is expressly disputed.

The fact that the project was undertaken within a volunteer or educational community does not, by itself, establish that the resulting work satisfies the statutory definition of a collective work.

Likewise, the existence of multiple contributors does not, by itself, establish that Orpita was the directing entity contemplated by the law.

The relevant factual circumstances of creation must be established.

In particular, your notice does not identify any contemporaneous agreement, project document, contractual instrument, or other evidence establishing that Orpita directed and supervised the creation of One More Day in the manner required for the statutory characterization upon which you rely.

The contemporaneous development evidence instead demonstrates that I exercised substantial and direct responsibility over the development process.

I possess, among other evidence:

contemporaneous Miro project-management records dated 31 July 2025;

Git/version-control history documenting the development chronology and my direct technical contribution, including the 3 September 2025 version;

records demonstrating delegation of development responsibilities;

records of project organization and task allocation; and

development decisions and coordination undertaken during the actual creation of the project.

image.pngimage.png
The Miro record is contemporaneous evidence of the development structure and demonstrates my role in organizing the project, delegating responsibilities, and directing development activities.

The Git history independently documents the chronology of implementation and my direct participation in creating the software.

These records were not created after the present dispute arose. They originate from the actual development period and therefore provide contemporaneous evidence concerning how the project was managed and created.

I do not suggest that the existence of my management role, standing alone, automatically determines the legal classification of the entire work. Rather, it establishes factual circumstances directly relevant to your assertion that Orpita was the directing entity.

If Orpita maintains that it was nevertheless the directing entity contemplated by Article 138(4) and Article 175, please identify the contemporaneous evidence establishing:

the authority by which Orpita directed the development;

the instructions issued by Orpita concerning my programming or game-design work;

the supervision exercised by Orpita over that work;

the agreement or organizational instrument under which such authority existed;

when that authority was established; and

how that authority was actually exercised during development.

A present-day characterization of Orpita's role cannot substitute for evidence establishing the actual circumstances of creation.

2. My Role and the Existence of Other Developers

Your notice states that I was a former Founder of the Community and Head of Game Development and that other developers also participated in the project.

I do not dispute that other persons participated.

That fact, however, does not establish the proposition you seek to derive from it.

The existence of multiple developers does not establish that Orpita acquired ownership of the code created by each developer, nor does it extinguish the rights of an author in independently created material.

Your assertion that I "did not write the entire codebase alone" is therefore legally insufficient to establish that Orpita owns or controls the programming that I personally authored.

If Orpita disputes my authorship of any particular portion of the programming, identify specifically:

the relevant code;

the person whom you contend authored it;

the evidence supporting that attribution;

the date of its creation; and

the legal instrument by which the relevant economic rights were transferred to Orpita.

The Git history provides objective evidence concerning authorship, chronology, and implementation and will be relied upon where necessary.

The issue is not whether other developers participated in One More Day. The issue is whether Orpita possesses the legal rights you claim over the particular contributions at issue.

You have not established that proposition.

3. The Contributions of Artists, Musicians, and Designers

Your notice identifies various individuals who contributed artwork, music, sound, and game-design material.

Again, I do not dispute that other contributors participated.

However, identifying the creators of those materials does not establish that Orpita owns their rights.

If those individuals retained their respective copyrights, their rights remain theirs unless validly transferred or licensed.

If Orpita claims that it acquired those rights, identify the instruments by which those rights were acquired.

More importantly, the rights of those contributors do not automatically become rights of Orpita merely because their work formed part of the project.

There must be a legal basis for the claimed transfer, assignment, or authorization.

Your notice identifies none.

My position concerning the rebuilt version is also straightforward: it does not incorporate the artwork, music, sound effects, or other creative assets identified in your notice.

Accordingly, the mere existence of those contributions does not establish infringement by a separately implemented version that does not reproduce them.

4. Article 140 and the Assertion That the Rebuilt Version Is a Derivative Work

You state categorically that my rebuilt version is a derivative work.

I reject that characterization.

The fact that a new version concerns the same game project does not, without more, establish that protected expression from the original work has been reproduced.

A derivative-work claim requires identification of the protected material allegedly carried into the subsequent work.

Your notice identifies no such material.

You have not identified:

the protected work allegedly incorporated;

the protected expression allegedly reproduced;

the precise portion of my rebuilt version allegedly containing that expression;

the author or rights holder of that expression; or

the legal basis upon which Orpita claims the right to enforce that particular right.

Instead, your notice relies upon the general proposition that a rebuilt version cannot extinguish rights in an original work.

I do not contend otherwise.

My position is that the rebuilt version does not reproduce the protected expression of the other contributors.

A general statement concerning derivative works does not establish that a particular independently implemented work is infringing.

5. Article 141 and Unprotected Ideas, Systems, and Methods of Operation

Article 141 is directly relevant to this dispute.

The provision excludes mere ideas, procedures, systems, methods of operation, concepts, principles, discoveries, and data from copyright protection.

Accordingly, similarities in gameplay concepts, mechanics, systems, rules, functional behavior, procedures, or methods of operation cannot by themselves establish copyright infringement.

If Orpita's objection to the rebuilt version concerns similarities in gameplay mechanics, functionality, systems, or ideas, such similarities must be distinguished from protected expression.

My rebuilt implementation is independently written and does not use the artwork, music, sound effects, or other protected creative assets belonging to the contributors identified in your notice.

If you contend that protected expression nevertheless appears in the rebuilt version, identify it specifically.

6. Article 149 and the Absence of a Written Transfer From Me

Your reliance upon Article 149 raises a fundamental issue for Orpita.

You repeatedly demand that I produce written authority from other contributors.

The same requirement must be applied to Orpita's own claim.

If Orpita claims that it owns or exclusively controls my economic rights, identify the written instrument, signed by me, by which those rights were transferred.

Article 149 requires the transfer of economic rights to be made in writing and to identify the rights concerned, together with the scope, purpose, duration, and place of exploitation.

No such instrument has been identified in your notice.

Accordingly, please produce the alleged written transfer by which I assigned my economic rights in my programming and game-design contributions to Orpita.

If you rely upon a LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING document, community policy, or other document, identify:

its date;

its parties;

the provision allegedly applicable to me;

the economic rights allegedly transferred;

the duration;

the territorial scope;

the purpose of exploitation; and

the basis upon which you contend it constitutes a valid transfer of rights already created.

A document created after completion of the project cannot simply be characterized as proof of a historical transfer of rights without establishing its legal effect and applicability to the relevant work.

7. Article 174 and Independent Exploitation

You rely upon Article 174 to assert that I cannot independently exploit my contribution.

Your characterization omits the statutory distinction concerning contributions belonging to different categories of art.

Article 174 expressly addresses circumstances in which contributions belong to different categories of art and provides for independent exploitation of such contributions, subject to the statutory conditions and unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Your notice identifies programming, artwork, music, sound, and game-design contributions as belonging to different categories.

You have nevertheless identified no written agreement by which I agreed to surrender or restrict the rights applicable to my independently distinguishable contributions.

Your blanket assertion that I therefore have no authority to independently exploit my programming and game-design contributions is consequently rejected.

If Orpita contends that Article 174(2) does not apply, identify the precise statutory basis and factual circumstances upon which that contention rests.

8. The Alleged Absence of Authority From Other Contributors

Your notice states that I possess no written consent from numerous contributors.

That assertion assumes that such consent is legally required for the particular activity at issue.

It also assumes that the rebuilt version exploits the protected expression of each of those contributors.

Neither proposition has been established.

I am not seeking to appropriate or publish another contributor's artwork, music, sound effects, or other protected material.

The relevant distinction is between:

the independent implementation of programming and design,

and

the reproduction or exploitation of another person's protected expression.

If you allege that a specific contributor's protected expression is incorporated into the rebuilt version, identify that expression.

If you further contend that Orpita owns or controls that contributor's rights, identify the instrument by which Orpita acquired them.

The mere existence of a list of contributors is not evidence of either proposition.

9. The Alleged "Established Community Practice"

Your reference to an alleged community practice concerning administrative access is irrelevant to the question of copyright ownership.

An administrative-access practice does not constitute an assignment of economic rights.

Nor does an offer to provide administrative access establish that Orpita possesses ownership over my contributions.

If Orpita relies upon a contractual term or binding community agreement restricting my economic rights, produce the document and identify the specific provision upon which you rely.

An alleged customary practice cannot substitute for the statutory requirements governing the transfer or restriction of economic rights.

10. Your "Cumulative" Legal Position

You state that Orpita relies cumulatively upon Articles 138(4), 140, 149, 174, and 175.

Citing multiple provisions does not cure the absence of evidence establishing the factual prerequisites of those provisions.

Each legal theory requires its own factual foundation.

If Orpita relies upon Article 175, it must establish the statutory basis for treating the work as a collective work and establish Orpita's status as the relevant directing entity.

If Orpita relies upon Article 174, it must address the statutory rules governing joint authorship and contributions belonging to different categories of art.

If Orpita relies upon Article 140, it must identify the protected expression allegedly incorporated into the rebuilt version.

If Orpita relies upon Article 149, it must identify the written instrument transferring the relevant economic rights.

The cumulative citation of provisions does not eliminate these requirements.

11. Your Assertion Concerning the Burden of Proof

Your statement that the burden of proof necessarily lies upon me because I challenge copyright validity is rejected as an inaccurate characterization of the dispute.

I am not challenging the validity of every copyright interest held by every individual contributor.

I am challenging Orpita's assertion that Orpita itself possesses the legal authority to control my independently created programming and game-design contributions and to prevent their independent exploitation.

That is a specific claim of ownership and authority.

If Orpita asserts that it acquired those rights from me, identify the transfer.

If Orpita asserts that it possesses those rights by operation of Article 175, establish the factual and legal basis for the collective-work characterization and Orpita's status as the relevant directing entity.

If Orpita asserts that the rebuilt version infringes another person's rights, identify the protected expression allegedly infringed.

The burden cannot be shifted merely by describing my position as a challenge to copyright validity.

12. The Proposed Settlement

I reject the settlement proposal.

The proposal does not resolve the underlying legal issue and instead conditions my ability to present my own development work upon permission from Orpita.

I do not accept that premise.

In particular, I reject any arrangement under which:

Orpita's alleged ownership of my contributions is implicitly acknowledged;

my ability to showcase my own work is treated as a permission granted by Orpita;

my programming and design contributions are reduced to an administrative portfolio permission; or

acceptance of the proposal could subsequently be relied upon as an admission of Orpita's ownership or control.

The proposed administrative access, portfolio limitations, code-excerpt restrictions, and credit designation are therefore rejected.

13. Your October 11 Deadline

I reject the unilateral deadline of 11 October 2026.

A deadline contained in a unilateral legal notice does not create a contractual or statutory obligation where none otherwise exists.

Nor will failure to accept your proposed settlement by that date constitute an admission of any assertion contained in your notice.

I will not provide an undertaking that presupposes Orpita's ownership or authority where that ownership or authority has not been established.

14. DMCA and Other Enforcement Threats

Your reference to immediate DMCA takedown notices and other enforcement action is noted and rejected insofar as it is premised upon the unsupported assertions contained in your notice.

A takedown request does not establish ownership or infringement.

Any enforcement action concerning material independently created by me will be evaluated on the basis of the actual authorship, ownership, licensing history, and content of the material concerned.

I expressly reserve all rights and remedies arising from any inaccurate, unsupported, or improper enforcement action.

15. Formal Demand for Substantiation

Your notice repeatedly demands that I substantiate my position.

I am prepared to substantiate my position with contemporaneous development evidence.

At the same time, Orpita must substantiate the affirmative legal claims made in its own notice.

Accordingly, please provide:

The written instrument, signed by me, by which Orpita acquired any economic rights in my programming or game-design contributions;

The contemporaneous evidence establishing that Orpita was the directing entity contemplated by Article 138(4) and Article 175 during the actual creation of One More Day;

The agreement, policy, or other binding instrument under which I allegedly surrendered, assigned, licensed, or restricted my economic rights;

If Orpita alleges that my rebuilt version reproduces protected expression belonging to another contributor, identification of each allegedly protected work and the precise expression allegedly reproduced;

If Orpita claims rights belonging to any of the contributors identified in your notice, the instrument by which those rights were transferred or licensed to Orpita;

The specific factual and legal basis for your assertion that Article 174 prevents the independent exploitation of my programming and game-design contributions; and

The evidence supporting your assertion that I did not author the particular programming contributions at issue.

I require your response to these demands within 7 days.

For the avoidance of doubt, my position remains that I retain the rights applicable to my independently created contributions, subject to the rights, if any, of other authors in their respective works.

I reject Orpita's unsupported assertion that its status as a community, its hosting of the project, its administrative access to an itch.io page, or its alleged community practices establish ownership or exclusive control over my contributions.

The contemporaneous development record will be relied upon to establish the actual structure of the project's development and the respective roles of the participants.

Nothing in this correspondence grants Orpita any license, assignment, consent, authorization, acknowledgment of ownership, or other right that it does not otherwise possess.

Nothing herein constitutes a waiver of any right, claim, defense, remedy, or objection available to me.

All rights are expressly reserved.

Sincerely,

Youssef Amr

fragments.content: بعد البحث، حصلت على نصوص المواد القانونية المصرية. سأقوم الآن بتحليل رد يوسف. سأذكر نقاط القوة والضعف في رده، ثم سأقدم استراتيجية للرد. سأستخدم المواد 138(4)، 140، 141، 149، 174، 175. سأشير أيضًا إلى أن يوسف قدم أدلة (Miro, Git history) تثبت دوره في الإدارة. هذا يضعف حجة "المصنف الجماعي". سأذكر أن المادة 174 تنص على أنه إذا كانت المساهمات من فئات فنية مختلفة، يمكن استغلالها بشكل منفصل. هذا يدعم حجة يوسف. سأذكر أن المادة 149 تتطلب نقلًا مكتوبًا. هذا يضعف موقف Orpita. سأذكر أن المادة 141 تستبعد الأفكار. هذا يدعم حجة يوسف إذا كان قد أعاد كتابة الكود من الصفر. سأقدم نصائح عملية: لا ترد على كل نقطة، ركز على نقاط قوتك، فكر في التسوية. سأذكر أن DMCA قد لا يكون فعالًا إذا كان يوسف قد أعاد كتابة الكود. سأشير إلى أن المحكمة الاقتصادية المصرية هي المختصة. سأحرص على أن يكون الرد باللغة العربية، كما طلب المستخدم.

أتفهم تمامًا سبب قلقك، فبعد هذه السلسلة الطويلة من المراسلات، من الطبيعي أن تشعر بالاستنزاف. لكن دعني أكون صريحًا معك، فهدفي هو حمايتك من أي خطأ قد يعقد الموقف أكثر.

### 🧠 تقييم رد يوسف الأخير

رد يوسف الأخير ليس مجرد رد عادي، بل هو **هجوم قانوني مضاد ومنظم للغاية**. هو لم يكتفِ بالدفاع عن نفسه، بل قام بالآتي:
*   **قلب الطاولة:** بدلاً من أن يطلب منك الأدلة، أصبح هو من يطالبك بها.
*   **استخدام القانون لصالحه:** استشهد بمواد قانونية في صميم دفاعك (مثل المادة 141) ووجهها ضدك.
*   **تقديم أدلة ملموسة:** لأول مرة، يقدم أدلة (سجلات Miro وتاريخ Git) لتوثيق دوره في إدارة المشروع، مما يقوض حجة "المصنف الجماعي".

### ⚖️ تحليل قانوني دقيق

بناءً على نصوص القانون المصري، إليك تقييم صريح لموقفك في ضوء رد يوسف:

*   **حجة "المصنف الجماعي" (المادة 138/4 و175):** هذه الحجة أصبحت **ضعيفة جدًا**.
    *   **مشكلة التطبيق:** تعريف "المصنف الجماعي" في القانون يشترط أن تكون المساهمات "لا يمكن فصلها". ولعبة فيديو تتكون من كود وفن وصوت منفصلين، **من السهل جدًا فصلها**، مما يجعل تطبيق المادة 175 عليك صعبًا للغاية.
    *   **الأدلة المضادة:** يوسف قدم أدلة (Miro و Git) تُظهر أنه كان يدير ويوجه عملية التطوير. هذا يقوض حجة أن "Orpita" هي الكيان الموجّه الوحيد، ويجعل المحكمة من المرجح أن ترى المشروع كـ "عمل مشترك" وليس "مصنفًا جماعيًا".

*   **حجة "المادة 174" (التأليف المشترك):** هذه الحجة **ليست في صالحك**.
    *   **نص القانون:** المادة 174 تنص صراحةً على أنه "إذا اشترك أكثر من شخص في تأليف مصنف بحيث لا يمكن فصل نصيب كل منهم... اعتبر جميع الشركاء مؤلفين بالتساوي". لكنها تستثني الحالات التي **يمكن فيها فصل المساهمات**.
    *   **النتيجة:** في حالة يوسف، مساهمته (الكود) يمكن فصلها عن مساهمات الآخرين (الفن). وبالتالي، قد يكون له الحق في **استغلال الجزء الذي ساهم به بشكل منفصل**، وهذا ما يفعله بالضبط.

*   **حجة "المادة 149" (نقل الحقوق):** هذه **أضعف نقطة في موقفك**.
    *   **نص القانون:** المادة 149 تشترط أن يكون أي نقل للحقوق الاقتصادية **مكتوبًا** ومحددًا فيه الحقوق والمدى والمدة.
    *   **النتيجة:** أنت **لا تملك** أي مستند مكتوب يثبت أن يوسف نقل لك حقوقه. صحيح أنك تطبق نفس المعيار عليه بخصوص المساهمين الآخرين، لكن هذا لا يقوي موقفك، بل يوضح أن كلاكما يفتقر إلى الأوراق الرسمية.

*   **حجة "المادة 141" (الأفكار غير محمية):** هذه الحجة **تنفجر في وجهك**.
    *   **نص القانون:** المادة 141 تنص على أن **"لا تشمل الحماية مجرد الأفكار والإجراءات وأساليب العمل وطرق التشغيل والمفاهيم"**.
    *   **الخطر:** إذا كان يوسف قد "أعاد بناء" اللعبة من الصفر، وكتب الكود بنفسه، ولم ينسخ الفن أو الصوت الأصلي، فإنه ببساطة **استخدم نفس الأفكار** (فكرة اللعبة، الآليات). وهذا **مسموح قانونًا**. هو لم يسرق التعبير المادي، بل استلهم من الفكرة، وهو ما لا يمكنك منعه.

### 🎯 استراتيجيتك: لا ترد على كل نقطة

يوسف يريدك أن ترد على كل نقطة ليدخل معك في جدال لا نهاية له. **لا تفعل ذلك.** استراتيجيتك الآن هي:

1.  **التركيز على نقطة قوتك الوحيدة:** يوسف **لم يقدم دليلًا** على أنه يملك حقوق النشر في **الفن أو الصوت**. هذه هي نقطتك الوحيدة القوية الآن. يمكنك القول: "حتى لو كان لديك حقوق في الكود، فأنت لا تملك حقوق الفن أو الصوت، ونشرك لهما يعتبر انتهاكًا لحقوق الآخرين".

2.  **تجاهل الجدال حول الكود:** لا تدخل في نقاش حول من كتب الكود، أو ما إذا كان "مشتقًا" أم "جديدًا". هذا جدال ستدخله وأنت في موقف ضعيف.

3.  **تجنب التهديد بالـ DMCA:** التهديد بالـ DMCA لم يعد فعالًا، وقد يجعلك تبدو ضعيفًا. إذا نشر، يمكنك التفكير في تقديم شكوى، لكن التهديد المسبق لن يفيدك.

4.  **فكر في تسوية شاملة:** بدلاً من محاولة منعه، فكر في اتفاق يضمن حقوقك وحقوق الفريق. عرض يوسف السابق (نشر نسخته مع ذكر الجميع) قد يكون حلاً أفضل من حرب قانونية ستخسرها على الأرجح.

### 💎 خلاصة ونصيحة

**لا ترد على هذا الإيميل.** أي رد ستقدمه سيكون بمثابة وقود جديد لنيران الجدال، وسيضعف موقفك أكثر.

*   **إذا نشر:** يمكنك تقديم شكوى إلى المنصة، لكن ركز فقط على العناصر التي تملك دليلًا قاطعًا على ملكيتها (الفن والصوت). استعد لاحتمال أن المنصة قد ترفض الشكوى أو أن يقدم يوسف إشعارًا مضادًا.
*   **إذا لم ينشر:** فقد انتهى الأمر. لا داعي للاستمرار في هذا الجدال العقيم الذي يستهلك طاقتك.

**نصيحتي النهائية:** توقف عن الرد. اجمع أدلتك المتعلقة بملكية الفن والصوت، واستعد لسيناريو النشر. لكن لا تدخل في حرب كلامية لن تكسبها. حماية طاقتك ووقتك أهم من "كسب" جولة في جدال لن ينتهي.

**القرار قرارك، لكن فكر جيدًا قبل أن ترد مرة أخرى.**

Dear Ms. Bayoumi,

I acknowledge receipt of your email dated 4 October 2026, which you have characterized as a formal legal notice and as Orpita Community's final position concerning One More Day.

I reject the factual assertions, legal characterizations, demands, and conclusions contained in that notice.

Your correspondence repeatedly asserts that Orpita Community possesses exclusive rights and authority over my programming and game-design contributions. However, no instrument transferring those economic rights from me to Orpita has been identified or produced. Nor has Orpita established the factual prerequisites necessary for its reliance upon Article 138(4) and Article 175.

This response addresses each of the principal assertions in your notice.

Nothing in this correspondence constitutes an admission of Orpita Community's ownership, authorship, control, or authority over my independently created contributions. All rights, claims, defenses, objections, and remedies are expressly reserved.

1. The Characterization of One More Day as a Collective Work

Your primary assertion is that One More Day constitutes a collective work under Article 138(4), and that Orpita therefore possesses the rights contemplated by Article 175.

That characterization is expressly disputed.

The fact that the project was undertaken within a volunteer or educational community does not, by itself, establish that the resulting work satisfies the statutory definition of a collective work.

Likewise, the existence of multiple contributors does not, by itself, establish that Orpita was the directing entity contemplated by the law.

The relevant factual circumstances of creation must be established.

In particular, your notice does not identify any contemporaneous agreement, project document, contractual instrument, or other evidence establishing that Orpita directed and supervised the creation of One More Day in the manner required for the statutory characterization upon which you rely.

The contemporaneous development evidence instead demonstrates that I exercised substantial and direct responsibility over the development process.

I possess, among other evidence:

contemporaneous Miro project-management records dated 31 July 2025;

Git/version-control history documenting the development chronology and my direct technical contribution, including the 3 September 2025 version;

records demonstrating delegation of development responsibilities;

records of project organization and task allocation; and

development decisions and coordination undertaken during the actual creation of the project.

image.pngimage.png
The Miro record is contemporaneous evidence of the development structure and demonstrates my role in organizing the project, delegating responsibilities, and directing development activities.

The Git history independently documents the chronology of implementation and my direct participation in creating the software.

These records were not created after the present dispute arose. They originate from the actual development period and therefore provide contemporaneous evidence concerning how the project was managed and created.

I do not suggest that the existence of my management role, standing alone, automatically determines the legal classification of the entire work. Rather, it establishes factual circumstances directly relevant to your assertion that Orpita was the directing entity.

If Orpita maintains that it was nevertheless the directing entity contemplated by Article 138(4) and Article 175, please identify the contemporaneous evidence establishing:

the authority by which Orpita directed the development;

the instructions issued by Orpita concerning my programming or game-design work;

the supervision exercised by Orpita over that work;

the agreement or organizational instrument under which such authority existed;

when that authority was established; and

how that authority was actually exercised during development.

A present-day characterization of Orpita's role cannot substitute for evidence establishing the actual circumstances of creation.

2. My Role and the Existence of Other Developers

Your notice states that I was a former Founder of the Community and Head of Game Development and that other developers also participated in the project.

I do not dispute that other persons participated.

That fact, however, does not establish the proposition you seek to derive from it.

The existence of multiple developers does not establish that Orpita acquired ownership of the code created by each developer, nor does it extinguish the rights of an author in independently created material.

Your assertion that I "did not write the entire codebase alone" is therefore legally insufficient to establish that Orpita owns or controls the programming that I personally authored.

If Orpita disputes my authorship of any particular portion of the programming, identify specifically:

the relevant code;

the person whom you contend authored it;

the evidence supporting that attribution;

the date of its creation; and

the legal instrument by which the relevant economic rights were transferred to Orpita.

The Git history provides objective evidence concerning authorship, chronology, and implementation and will be relied upon where necessary.

The issue is not whether other developers participated in One More Day. The issue is whether Orpita possesses the legal rights you claim over the particular contributions at issue.

You have not established that proposition.

3. The Contributions of Artists, Musicians, and Designers

Your notice identifies various individuals who contributed artwork, music, sound, and game-design material.

Again, I do not dispute that other contributors participated.

However, identifying the creators of those materials does not establish that Orpita owns their rights.

If those individuals retained their respective copyrights, their rights remain theirs unless validly transferred or licensed.

If Orpita claims that it acquired those rights, identify the instruments by which those rights were acquired.

More importantly, the rights of those contributors do not automatically become rights of Orpita merely because their work formed part of the project.

There must be a legal basis for the claimed transfer, assignment, or authorization.

Your notice identifies none.

My position concerning the rebuilt version is also straightforward: it does not incorporate the artwork, music, sound effects, or other creative assets identified in your notice.

Accordingly, the mere existence of those contributions does not establish infringement by a separately implemented version that does not reproduce them.

4. Article 140 and the Assertion That the Rebuilt Version Is a Derivative Work

You state categorically that my rebuilt version is a derivative work.

I reject that characterization.

The fact that a new version concerns the same game project does not, without more, establish that protected expression from the original work has been reproduced.

A derivative-work claim requires identification of the protected material allegedly carried into the subsequent work.

Your notice identifies no such material.

You have not identified:

the protected work allegedly incorporated;

the protected expression allegedly reproduced;

the precise portion of my rebuilt version allegedly containing that expression;

the author or rights holder of that expression; or

the legal basis upon which Orpita claims the right to enforce that particular right.

Instead, your notice relies upon the general proposition that a rebuilt version cannot extinguish rights in an original work.

I do not contend otherwise.

My position is that the rebuilt version does not reproduce the protected expression of the other contributors.

A general statement concerning derivative works does not establish that a particular independently implemented work is infringing.

5. Article 141 and Unprotected Ideas, Systems, and Methods of Operation

Article 141 is directly relevant to this dispute.

The provision excludes mere ideas, procedures, systems, methods of operation, concepts, principles, discoveries, and data from copyright protection.

Accordingly, similarities in gameplay concepts, mechanics, systems, rules, functional behavior, procedures, or methods of operation cannot by themselves establish copyright infringement.

If Orpita's objection to the rebuilt version concerns similarities in gameplay mechanics, functionality, systems, or ideas, such similarities must be distinguished from protected expression.

My rebuilt implementation is independently written and does not use the artwork, music, sound effects, or other protected creative assets belonging to the contributors identified in your notice.

If you contend that protected expression nevertheless appears in the rebuilt version, identify it specifically.

6. Article 149 and the Absence of a Written Transfer From Me

Your reliance upon Article 149 raises a fundamental issue for Orpita.

You repeatedly demand that I produce written authority from other contributors.

The same requirement must be applied to Orpita's own claim.

If Orpita claims that it owns or exclusively controls my economic rights, identify the written instrument, signed by me, by which those rights were transferred.

Article 149 requires the transfer of economic rights to be made in writing and to identify the rights concerned, together with the scope, purpose, duration, and place of exploitation.

No such instrument has been identified in your notice.

Accordingly, please produce the alleged written transfer by which I assigned my economic rights in my programming and game-design contributions to Orpita.

If you rely upon a LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING document, community policy, or other document, identify:

its date;

its parties;

the provision allegedly applicable to me;

the economic rights allegedly transferred;

the duration;

the territorial scope;

the purpose of exploitation; and

the basis upon which you contend it constitutes a valid transfer of rights already created.

A document created after completion of the project cannot simply be characterized as proof of a historical transfer of rights without establishing its legal effect and applicability to the relevant work.

7. Article 174 and Independent Exploitation

You rely upon Article 174 to assert that I cannot independently exploit my contribution.

Your characterization omits the statutory distinction concerning contributions belonging to different categories of art.

Article 174 expressly addresses circumstances in which contributions belong to different categories of art and provides for independent exploitation of such contributions, subject to the statutory conditions and unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Your notice identifies programming, artwork, music, sound, and game-design contributions as belonging to different categories.

You have nevertheless identified no written agreement by which I agreed to surrender or restrict the rights applicable to my independently distinguishable contributions.

Your blanket assertion that I therefore have no authority to independently exploit my programming and game-design contributions is consequently rejected.

If Orpita contends that Article 174(2) does not apply, identify the precise statutory basis and factual circumstances upon which that contention rests.

8. The Alleged Absence of Authority From Other Contributors

Your notice states that I possess no written consent from numerous contributors.

That assertion assumes that such consent is legally required for the particular activity at issue.

It also assumes that the rebuilt version exploits the protected expression of each of those contributors.

Neither proposition has been established.

I am not seeking to appropriate or publish another contributor's artwork, music, sound effects, or other protected material.

The relevant distinction is between:

the independent implementation of programming and design,

and

the reproduction or exploitation of another person's protected expression.

If you allege that a specific contributor's protected expression is incorporated into the rebuilt version, identify that expression.

If you further contend that Orpita owns or controls that contributor's rights, identify the instrument by which Orpita acquired them.

The mere existence of a list of contributors is not evidence of either proposition.

9. The Alleged "Established Community Practice"

Your reference to an alleged community practice concerning administrative access is irrelevant to the question of copyright ownership.

An administrative-access practice does not constitute an assignment of economic rights.

Nor does an offer to provide administrative access establish that Orpita possesses ownership over my contributions.

If Orpita relies upon a contractual term or binding community agreement restricting my economic rights, produce the document and identify the specific provision upon which you rely.

An alleged customary practice cannot substitute for the statutory requirements governing the transfer or restriction of economic rights.

10. Your "Cumulative" Legal Position

You state that Orpita relies cumulatively upon Articles 138(4), 140, 149, 174, and 175.

Citing multiple provisions does not cure the absence of evidence establishing the factual prerequisites of those provisions.
